title: Energy in Collisions
seo_title: Grade 4 Collisions Worksheets: How Energy Moves When Objects Hit
standard_text: Ask questions and predict outcomes about the changes in energy that occur when objects collide.
meta_desc: Free Grade 4 science worksheets on energy in collisions (NGSS 4-PS3-3): energy moving between objects, sound, heat and changes of shape, and faster collisions with data tables. 100 practice questions with answers.
key_big: In a collision, energy moves between the objects.
key_sub: The moving object slows down and the object it hits speeds up. Some energy changes into sound and heat.
body_html:
How to think about it

When objects collide, energy moves between them. The moving object slows down, and the object it hits gets energy and starts to move.

Some energy also changes into sound (a bang or click), heat (things get a little warmer) and changes of shape (dents). Energy is not destroyed. A faster collision moves more energy: louder sounds, bigger dents and objects pushed farther.

Example

A cue ball hits a pool ball at rest. What happens?

Energy moves from the cue ball to the pool ball.

The cue ball slows; the pool ball moves.

Answer: The pool ball moves and the cue ball slows down.

Example

Two cars bump. You hear a crash. What does the sound show?

Some energy changed into sound.

Answer: Energy changed form.

Common mistakes

  • Thinking energy disappears in a crash. It moves or changes form.
  • Thinking the object that is hit gets no energy.
  • Forgetting sound and heat as ways energy leaves a collision.

faq.q: What happens to energy when objects collide?
faq.a: Energy moves from the moving object to the object it hits. Some changes into sound, heat and changes of shape. None is destroyed.

faq.q: Why does a faster collision make a louder sound?
faq.a: A faster object has more energy, so more energy can change into sound.

faq.q: Why do helmets and bumpers have soft parts?
faq.a: Soft materials change shape and take in energy, so less energy reaches your head or the people in a car.

items.q: Where does some energy go when two cars bump?
c: into sound, heat and bending the metal
items.e: Energy is not destroyed; it changes into other forms.

items.q: A hammer hits a nail. Where does the hammer's energy go?
c: into pushing the nail into the wood, sound and heat
items.e: The nail moves, you hear a bang and the nail gets warm.

items.q: A bumper car hits a parked bumper car. What happens to the parked car?
c: It moves backward toward the bumper car.
It gives all its energy to the bumper car.
Nothing happens; it gets no energy.
It gets energy and starts to move.
items.e: Energy is transferred from the moving object to the object it hits.

items.q: Why do car bumpers crumple in a crash?
c: Changing shape uses up some of the energy, so less reaches the people inside.
items.e: Crumple zones turn energy into changing the car's shape.

items.q: Is energy destroyed in a collision?
c: No. It moves to other objects or changes into sound and heat.
items.e: Energy changes form or moves; it is not destroyed.

items.q: What is a collision?
c: when an object is at rest
when two objects hit each other
when an object stops by itself
items.e: Balls, cars and bowling pins collide when they hit each other.

items.q: A bumper car hits a parked bumper car, and you hear a bump. What does this show?
items.e: When objects collide, energy moves to the other object or changes into sound, heat or a change of shape.
